sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Block Puzzle is a physics-based puzzle game that requires players to rotate and drop blocks into place to create a solid line without gaps. The game starts with a grid of empty spaces, and as you progress through the levels, the grid will get smaller, and the blocks will get smaller, making it increasingly difficult to create a solid line.

The game has several core mechanics that make it so engaging and challenging. First, the blocks come in different shapes and sizes, each with its own unique properties. Some blocks are larger and easier to rotate, while others are smaller and harder to manipulate. The blocks also have different weights, which affect how far they fall when dropped.

Another key mechanic is the game's physics engine, which simulates the way the blocks behave in mid-air. When you drop a block, it will fall until it reaches the bottom of the grid or collides with another block. The physics engine makes the game feel realistic and unpredictable, adding an extra layer of challenge and excitement to the gameplay.

Finally, the game has a limited amount of undo moves, which forces players to think carefully about each move before making it. This adds a sense of urgency and pressure to the gameplay, making it even more engaging and challenging.

sections.heading: Beginner Tips and Tricks
sections.body:
If you're new to Block Puzzle, here are a few beginner tips and tricks to get you started:

First, start with the basics. Take some time to get familiar with the game's controls and mechanics. Practice rotating and dropping blocks, and get a feel for how they behave in mid-air.

Next, focus on creating a solid line without gaps. Pay attention to the blocks' shapes and sizes, and try to use them to your advantage.

Finally, don't be afraid to undo moves. The game's limited undo feature can be a lifesaver when you make a mistake, and it's always better to be safe than sorry.

Other tips include:

* Use the blocks' weights to your advantage. Lighter blocks will fall faster, while heavier blocks will fall slower.
* Try to create a solid line as early as possible. The farther you go, the harder it gets.
* Don't worry too much about the gaps at first. Focus on creating a solid line, and then worry about filling in the gaps later.

Next, use the game's physics engine to your advantage. Pay attention to how the blocks behave in mid-air, and use that knowledge to your advantage. For example, you can use a block's momentum to carry it into a gap, or use a block's weight to slow it down.

Finally, practice, practice, practice. The more you play, the more you'll learn about the game's mechanics and how to manipulate the blocks to your advantage.

* Using the game's undo feature to your advantage. You can use it to recover from mistakes, or to try out different strategies and see what works best.
